title: Copilot Cowork: access Business Applications through Work IQ and use business skills
summary: The briefing's rollout facts, admin-installed default, consumption billing and documented controls are supported. The App Access Control route reaches the correct control but should explain the remaining application-selection step.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans access to Business Applications through Work IQ in Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote: Users can access Business Applications through Work IQ in Copilot Cowork

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Business Skills completing end-to-end business processes grounded in enterprise data and apps.
claims.quote: use Business Skills to complete end-to-end business processes grounded in their enterprise data and apps.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365), Microsoft Dataverse and Work IQ.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Microsoft Dataverse", "Work IQ"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: December CY2026 is the roadmap target, not a committed availability date.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"; "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The Business apps plugin connects Cowork with Dynamics 365, Dataverse and Power Apps information and processes.
claims.quote: With Business Applications in Work IQ, you can ask Cowork practical questions across your Dataverse, Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Service, and custom Power Apps data.

claims.claim: Business Applications access through Cowork is in public preview.
claims.quote: Access through Cowork is available in public preview.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Cowork examples include creating a follow-up task for an account owner.
claims.quote: Create a follow-up task for the account owner

claims.claim: Microsoft's Cowork examples include reassigning account ownership.
claims.quote: Reassign account ownership

claims.claim: Microsoft's Cowork examples include escalating a case.
claims.quote: Escalate the service issue for an unresolved case

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in because users cannot add the Business apps plugin until an administrator installs it.
claims.quote: An admin must install the Business apps (preview) plugin for users. Users can't add the plugin in Cowork until an admin installs it for them.

claims.claim: Plugin installation can target All users or Specific users and groups.
claims.quote: In the Installed for field, select All users or Specific users and groups.

claims.claim: Power Apps model-driven apps are available as Business Applications in Work IQ.
claims.quote: Power Apps model-driven apps are available as Business Applications in Work IQ.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses an app's views, forms and tables to complete a request.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses the app's views, forms, and tables to complete the request.

claims.claim: Business skills are business-process instructions saved in a Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: Provide your business process information. ... The business skill is saved in the environment you used to connect to the Dataverse MCP server or a relevant environment through Work IQ.

claims.claim: After activation, Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork and connected agents can discover and use business skills the user can access.
claims.quote: After you create and activate business skills in your environment, Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, and connected agents can discover and use the skills you have access to and follow your organization's processes.

claims.claim: Business Applications access through Work IQ MCP is generally available.
claims.quote: Access to Business Applications through Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Microsoft Copilot Studio is generally available.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments, subject to exceptions.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: Default enablement for existing environments was deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule. Check this article for updates.

claims.claim: All users is the default tenant audience option.
claims.quote: To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Cowork respects the user's existing permissions when returning business data and offering actions.
claims.quote: Cowork respects the role-based access and permissions already set by your organization, so it only shows information and offers actions that you are authorized to use.

claims.claim: Work IQ does not grant extra access to business data.
claims.quote: Work IQ doesn't grant additional access to business data.

claims.claim: For US tenants using FedRAMP-accredited environments, enabling Work IQ might send data outside the FedRAMP authorization boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.claim: Plugin connection setup includes selecting credentials and entering the displayed sign-in number in Authenticator.
claims.quote: Select your credentials. A number appears to approve your sign in request. ... Enter the number in the Authenticator app.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: App Access controls which applications, including Copilot Cowork, can access an environment's data.
claims.quote: App Access is the mechanism used to choose which applications, including agentic applications such as Copilot Cowork, are allowed to access data in a particular environment.

claims.claim: Business skills are user-owned by default.
claims.quote: Skills are user-owned by default.

claims.claim: A business skill can be shared with everyone in its environment.
claims.quote: General access—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.

claims.claim: Security-role-based skill access requires both the shared-to security role and Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role, either directly or through a team. Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ supports creating business records.
claims.quote: create a record with the values in your prompt

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ supports updating existing business records.
claims.quote: or update an existing record.

claims.claim: Users review proposed changes and explicitly confirm an operation before it is submitted.
claims.quote: For an operation that changes data, review the proposed values, make any needed changes, and explicitly confirm the operation before it's submitted.

claims.claim: Delete operations also require explicit confirmation.
claims.quote: Delete operations also require explicit confirmation.

claims.claim: Users can create business skills through Copilot or a connected agent.
claims.quote: You can also create and update skills through Copilot or an agent connected to Work IQ or the Dataverse MCP server

claims.claim: Users can update business skills through Copilot or a connected agent.
claims.quote: Ask your agent to create a new business skill or update an existing one.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing skills with repeatable scenarios before sharing them broadly.
claims.quote: Test each skill with a repeatable scenario before you share it broadly.

claims.claim: Create and update operations are unavailable when the selected form uses JavaScript OnLoad, OnChange or OnSave handlers.
claims.quote: You can't create or update a record when the selected form has JavaScript OnLoad, OnChange, or OnSave event handlers.

claims.claim: Custom controls are not supported.
claims.quote: Custom controls and subgrids aren't supported.

claims.claim: Subgrids are not supported.
claims.quote: Custom controls and subgrids aren't supported.

claims.claim: The Business skills page does not currently display per-skill runtime usage or feedback.
claims.quote: The Business skills page doesn't currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback. Use controlled test cases and any logs or traces provided by the agent experience to collect evidence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Business context used in Cowork is consumption-billed as part of Cowork rather than a separate Business Applications category.
claims.quote: Business context accessed through Cowork contributes to Cowork consumption. ... Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.where: front matter: cost and licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cost is variable consumption measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences. ... Complexity, the context needed, and the work performed affect consumption.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity packs can fund consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription can fund consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Separately reported Work IQ API consumption is not a Business Applications-only breakdown.
claims.quote: Work IQ API consumption can include both Microsoft 365 productivity context and business applications context. Its total is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps, so a prompt is not a fixed-price operation.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature documentation publishes no per-task Copilot Credit rate for Cowork requests using business context.
claims.quote: Searched: Business apps preview Cowork plugin license pricing per task Copilot Credits. Read understand-costs, plugins/cost-considerations and Work IQ API licensing; the Cowork credit-usage FAQ says task cost cannot be checked in advance. No fixed per-task rate found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft names no separate license for the Business apps plugin itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Business apps preview Cowork plugin license pricing per task Copilot Credits. Read cowork-work-iq, cowork-manage-plugins, cost-considerations and Work IQ API licensing. Plugin guidance names Microsoft 365 Copilot user licenses, not a separate Business apps plugin license.

claims.claim: The Cowork experience can vary with the organization's apps, licenses, policies and available services.
claims.quote: Some experiences might vary based on your organization's apps, licenses, policies, and available services.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; controls[4].governs
claims.claim: Spending policies covering Cowork can cap consumption using policy and per-user limits.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: Underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during consumption-based previews.
claims.quote: For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: Users need permission to the Power Platform environment involved in a request.
claims.quote: You need permission to access the Power Platform environment, model-driven app, and business data involved in your request.

claims.claim: Users need permission to the model-driven app involved in a request.
claims.quote: You need permission to access the Power Platform environment, model-driven app, and business data involved in your request.

claims.claim: Users need permission to the business data involved in a request.
claims.quote: You need permission to access the Power Platform environment, model-driven app, and business data involved in your request.

claims.claim: The documented prerequisites require a Power Platform administrator to enable Work IQ for the environment.
claims.quote: A Power Platform administrator must enable Work IQ for the environment in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps must be Default or On.
claims.quote: For the model-driven app, the Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps setting (m365copilotmodelappenabled) must be set to Default or On.

claims.claim: Microsoft names AI Administrator for Microsoft 365 availability settings.
claims.quote: AI Administrator role to work with settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft names Power Platform Administrator for environment participation and application-access settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator to configure environment settings.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is not currently available in sovereign or government clouds, including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.claim: The install route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > Business apps (preview) > Install.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... In the Name column, select Business apps (preview). ... In the Business apps (preview) panel, select the Install button.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} updates the catalog package's deployment audience.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} ... deployedTo ... Enum value indicating the deployment scope of the package.

claims.claim: The package update request uses deployedTo for deployment scope.
claims.quote: deployedTo ... Enum value indicating the deployment scope of the package. Required if updating acquireUsersAndGroups.

claims.claim: The package update request uses acquireUsersAndGroups for the target users and groups.
claims.quote: acquireUsersAndGroups ... Users/groups for whom the package is deployed.

claims.claim: The Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The package update operation is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The audience setting is under Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings. ... In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: No API for the tenant Business Applications audience setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications Work IQ tenant setting API Microsoft Graph Dataverse CopilotSettings; "Business Applications data" "Graph" settings API. Read default-settings, manage-ai-experience-access and quickstart. No matching tenant-setting API found.

claims.claim: The audience choices include Specific groups and No users as well as All users.
claims.quote: To turn off access for everyone, select No users. ... To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups, and then add or remove groups.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ is controlled under Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: Select Manage, and select the environment. ... Select Settings > Product > Features. ... Locate Work IQ. ... Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: No API for the environment Work IQ setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment enable API Dataverse organization; "Work IQ" "Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment"; "Work IQ" "pac admin"; "Work IQ" "Power Platform API". Read participation guidance and searched organization reference for intelligence, Work IQ and semantic: no matching setting.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.claim: Security > Identity & access > App Access Control > environment > Enable reaches App Access Control in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Select Enable, and then select Save. ... Return to the environment and select the applications you want to block from accessing the environment.
claims.fix: Keep the cited route and append to controls[3].note: 'After enabling and saving, return to the environment and select the applications to block.' The cited feature page gives this remaining step. The general control-app-access-environment page instead documents Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled, then application > Block; acknowledge that alternate documented UI.

claims.claim: PATCH https://<organization>/api/data/v9.2/applications(<applicationid>) can update an application's access setting.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /applications(applicationid) ... Writable columns/attributes ... Access ... LogicalName ... access

claims.claim: An application access request-body value of 0 means Allowed.
claims.quote: LogicalName | access ... Access Choices/Options ... 0 | Allowed

claims.claim: An application access request-body value of 1 means Blocked.
claims.quote: Access Choices/Options ... 1 | Blocked

claims.claim: Changing an application's access status does not separately enable environment-level enforcement.
claims.quote: If you set some apps to Allowed or Blocked, you don't need to remove the setting when the app access control feature is turned off to Disabled. There are no app restrictions in this environment.

claims.claim: General App Access documentation requires a managed environment.
claims.quote: Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.claim: Spending limits are under Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Spending limits.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... Spending limits

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates spending policy limits.
claims.quote: PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} ... The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: The spending policy update request uses periodLimit for the policy limit.
claims.quote: "periodLimit": { "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.limitedCostManagementQuantity", "value": 10000, "unit": "copilotCredit" }

claims.claim: The spending policy update request uses perUserLimit for the per-user limit.
claims.quote: "perUserLimit": { "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.limitedCostManagementQuantity", "value": 500, "unit": "copilotCredit" }

claims.claim: The spending policy update operation is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Spending policies cover selected users and services rather than a dedicated Business Applications category.
claims.quote: Spending policies let you choose the users and services covered, set a shared monthly limit, add a per-user limit, and receive alerts as consumption approaches a threshold.

claims.claim: A skill can be deactivated under Power Apps > environment > More > Business skills > skill > Deactivate.
claims.quote: Go to Power Apps and select your environment. ... select More, and then select Business skills. ... Select a skill, and then select Deactivate from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.claim: PATCH /skills(<skillid>) can deactivate a business skill by updating its state and status.
claims.quote: SetState ... PATCH /skills(skillid) ... Update the statecode and statuscode properties.

claims.claim: Setting statecode to 1 selects the Inactive business skill state.
claims.quote: statecode Choices/Options ... 1 | Label: Inactive DefaultStatus: 2 InvariantName: Inactive

claims.claim: Setting statuscode to 2 selects the Inactive status reason.
claims.quote: statuscode Choices/Options ... 2 | Label: Inactive State:1 TransitionData: None

claims.claim: Deactivation stops skill discovery and use without deleting the skill's content or history.
claims.quote: To stop agents from discovering or using an active skill: ... Select a skill, and then select Deactivate ... Deactivating a skill preserves its content and version history.

claims.claim: Sharing is available through Share for a selected skill on the Business skills page.
claims.quote: Select a skill, and then select Share from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.claim: Enabling an experience does not itself grant business-data access.
claims.quote: Enabling an experience doesn't grant access to business data.

claims.claim: The Package Management API documents blocking a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.

claims.claim: The package block operation is a beta API.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The package block operation prevents usage rather than installing or uninstalling a plugin.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly identify a Business apps (preview) package in the Package Management API documentation, so its tenant catalog package must first be identified.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Package Management API plugins catalog Cowork; Cowork Business apps plugin Work IQ MCP server block package catalog API. Read package overview, update and block references and Cowork plugin management; general plugin coverage is documented, no feature-specific package ID is given.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP availability control applies to the whole server.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP server can be blocked under Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools. ... Select Work IQ MCP. ... To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether blocking the Work IQ MCP server also stops the Business apps plugin in Cowork.
claims.quote: Searched: Cowork Business apps plugin Work IQ MCP server block; "Business apps" "Cowork" "MCP" "Block". Read manage-ai-experience-access, cowork-work-iq, cowork-manage-plugins and business-applications-work-iq. No explicit dependency or blocking outcome for this plugin was stated.
